newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade at $66, up $1 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade at $66, up $1 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold after midday Tuesday at $66.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from last week's top price, according to feedlot sources.

Cattle sold early at $65.00 in light volume, but moved $1.00 higher after midday following gains in wholesale beef prices and a jump in Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures, sources said. CME traders said futures were partly bolstered by talk that some cattle had traded at $65.25.
By mid-afternoon, about 5,000 head total had sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 1,000 in Kansas at prices ranging from $65.00 to $66.00, sources said.
Total sales were seen expanding by the end of the day, they said.

Strength also stemmed from steady to smaller showlists this week and weight gains that have been curbed by extremely cold weather, with more frigid temperatures expected Friday through Monday, cattle feeders said.

Below-zero wind chills were reported as late as early Tuesday in the Panhandle before temperatures moderated in the afternoon. Temperatures were expected in the mid-40's Wednesday, but winds were seen blowing 15 to 20 mph in much of the Panhandle and western Oklahoma, forecasters said.
Gains were posted in boxed beef values at midday, with USDA reporting cut-out values up $0.75 to $1.03 per cwt compared with Monday's closes.
Also, CME live cattle futures closed 0.400 cent a lb higher to 0.050 cent lower with February up 0.400 cent at 65.975 cents per lb.
